text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Kenyan government maintains its hardline stance towards constitutional reforms with President Daniel arap Moi blaming the opposition for chaos on Monday: Moi tells foreign missions not to meddle in the country's affairs.
- Protestant churches jointly back the call by Roman Catholic bishops for an immediate start to the constitutional reform process.

- Various organisations and individuals condemn the suspension of two top Kenya News Television Network news editors on Wednesday saying it showed the determination of the Kenyan government to cover-up police brutality.
- Four people die during a shoot-out involving police officers and suspected car-jackers in the outskirts of Nairobi.
- Official Opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa writes to President Moi asking for urgent dialogue.
- The Minister for Foreign Affairs Kalonzo Musyoka urges the United States government to refrain from apportioning blame over the recent violence.
- Businessman Kamlesh Pattni denies rumours that he had taken advantage of the unrest on Monday to flee the country.
- The writing is on the wall. Calls for constitutional reforms by the opposition is the biggest challenge President Moi has faced in pluralist Kenya.
- Opposition leader Kenneth Matiba calls on all opposition leaders to boycott the forthcoming general elections if constitutional reform calls are not enacted.
